next_step: Finish POC latency runbook, SE follow-up demo on streaming perf (target week of 2024-10-18), share Dedicated pricing scenarios
summary: Mid-market SaaS product team evaluating Redwood Hosted API for outbound SDR/chat agents; strong interest in migrating to Dedicated if latency, cost, and SLA needs met. Main ask: streaming + tool-calling (CRM/email/calendar) with sub-200ms token latency for interactive agent flows and predictable throughput for 50-150 concurrent SDR bots.
notes: 2024-07-10: Aisha intro call with CPO (Jared Bloom) + Head of Product (Lina Cho). Initial interest: outbound chat agents that can take actions in CRM and calendar.
Use-case detail: 'We want assistants that can triage leads, send sequences, and book meetings — tool calls need to be synchronous and fast; no visible lag to reps.'
Latency SLOs discussed: target ~150-250ms per token p50, p95 under 400-500ms for streaming; end-to-end user-visible response time <1s for short replies.

Throughput: typical daily concurrency 40-80 agents during peak; want headroom for 120 concurrent during promos. Average prompt + context ~1200 tokens; expected regen/step usage minimal but caching critical.

POC plan (kicked off 2024-09-20): staged - 1) demo with streaming + tool-calling (actions to SFDC/Gmail/Calendar) 2) 2-week synthetic load test (p95/p99) 3) 2-week limited live pilot with 10 SDRs 4) pricing + Dedicated sizing exercise.

POC results (2024-10-03 bench): Hosted API streaming achieved p50 ~140ms/token, p95 ~360ms under our test harness; p99 spikes when batch/windowing not enabled. Observed benefits from prefix caching on common prompts.
Security/Compliance: asked for SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML integration for engineers, audit logs for tool calls, optional KMS for customer key management, data residency note for EU customers in roadmap.

Integration needs: tool calling to Salesforce (create task, update lead status), Gmail send + thread link, Google Calendar invite creation with attendee availability check; must support idempotency and audit trail for every agent action.

Cost sensitivity: mid-market procurement — wants clear Hosted API unit economics before committing to Dedicated; forecasted ARR range $150k-$300k — Dedicated pricing must show 25-40% TCO improvement for steady state.
Quote from Head of Product: 'If the streaming feels instant and tool calls are reliable, we can flip to Dedicated within 2 quarters.'
Security review: security questionnaire sent 2024-08-02; partial responses returned, outstanding items on KMS & legal for data residency (open).

Open tech questions: how Redwood handles graceful fallback (model variant) when Dedicated capacity is saturated; routing policies for latency-first vs cost-first tenants; telemetry hooks for tracing per-tool-call latency.
Next demo scheduled: 2024-10-18 with SE to run live streaming scenarios + simulated calendar/CRM actions (action failure modes included).
Internal notes: prioritize optimizing batching/windowing and prefix caching suggestions from Redwood Optimize; add evals for hallucination on tool outputs (must not fabricate calendar invites).
Sales cadence: AE weekly syncs until procurement; legal kickoff after security Q complete.
